result.title: The women’s health gap should not exist. Here’s how to close it
result.description:
Just 6% of private #healthcare funding goes towards women’s health, and across multiple diseases affecting both sexes, only 3% of studies look at how those diseases affect women.

As a result, women are diagnosed late for more than 700 conditions - and spend 25% more of their lives in poorer health than men, a study by the World Economic Forum and McKinsey found.

These statistics are shocking - but they’re not set in stone, says Paula Bellostas, Healthcare Global Lead at Kearney and a co-author of a new World Economic Forum paper on women’s #health innovation. She says that closing the women’s health gap means bringing gender into research right from the outset - and women advocating for themselves as patients.

The Women’s Health Innovation Radar, produced in collaboration with the Kearney Health Institute, Gates Foundation, Wellcome Leap and the World Economic Forum’s Global Alliance For Women's Health, maps the biggest advances - and remaining gaps - across the full science-to-patient journey. Read it here: https://www.weforum.org/publications/the-women-s-health-innovation-radar-revealing-gaps-and-opportunities-across-the-science-to-patient-journey/

result.title: AI's real impact on jobs - what it means for you, your company and future generations
result.description:
Artificial intelligence is already having an impact on the way most of us work - but it’s still early days and it's hard to predict exactly which jobs will disappear completely, what new ones will be created, and when and where this will happen.
It’s a subject that's important to all of us - so my colleague Gayle Markovitz spoke to the head of an AI services firm, Ravi Kumar of Cognizant, and to the head of the World Economic Forum’s Centre for the New Economy and Society, Saadia Zahidi. Both have unique insights into the impact of AI on the economy, on employment, and the implications for education and training.

result.title: This start-up wants to provide sunlight at night with mirrored satellites
result.description:
Reflect Orbital is developing satellites with 'giant mirrors' designed to reflect sunlight back to specific locations on Earth after dark.

The company says the technology could power #solar farms at night, provide low-carbon lighting during emergencies and even extend farms' growing seasons.

The technology is still at the experimental stage, and its wider implications remain under debate.

The World Economic Forum’s Future of Space Community serves as a platform for public-private cooperation, uniting experts from business, government and academia to explore the responsible and sustainable development of space technologies. Learn more: https://initiatives.weforum.org/future-space-community/home

result.title: Can business help nature win?
result.description:
Can businesses make more money by restoring nature? According to new research, the answer is yes.

New research has found 50 ways that businesses in areas that span the range of business itself (think everything from fashion to agriculture to recycling to mining) can both make money and leave nature better-off. The research discovered that globally, $7 trillion is spent every year destroying nature, and only about $200 billion protecting it.

Laura Fisher leads the World Economic Forum's work on nature-positive industries.

Here she breaks down the practical (and simple) ways businesses can grow while giving back to nature.

Read about all 50 Investible Opportunities for a New Nature Economy here: https://www.weforum.org/publications/50-investible-opportunities-for-a-new-nature-economy-insight-report/

result.title: Jaguar Conservation & How Quantum Computing Impacts Data Security | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:12 - How quantum computing impacts data security:
The world is counting down to Q-Day, when quantum computers will be so powerful that they can break the #encryption that keeps your private data safe. Hackers know this is coming, so they are stockpiling data now that they can use in the future to manipulate individuals or compromise national security, says Rebecca Krauthamer, CEO and Co-Founder of cybersecurity company QuSecure. Here, she talks us through the dangers to privacy posed by the arrival of quantum computing, and explains what we can do to keep our data safe.

03:43 - How young people are tackling plastic pollution:
Global Shapers Semina Šatara, Li Weijie and Valentina Velasquez Portnoy unveil the out-of-the-box solutions they’ve found for beating plastic #pollution, from clean-ups that go viral to mapping #plastic sources through citizen science.

07:34 - Ex-racing driver leads jaguar conservation:
Mário Haberfeld used to race cars for Jaguar Brazil Racing. Today he champions the conservation of jaguars in Brazil and around the world. Haberfeld's charity, Onçafari, has pioneered a way to reintroduce #jaguars into the wild. A successful project in Brazil’s Pantanal, the world’s biggest wetland, has also brought an #ecotourism boom to the area and given the world a blueprint for big cat conservation. Here’s how they did it.
